text:
Paula: FYI we started seeing a big uptick in 5xx/gateway errors right after the 16:07 canary push (r-2026-03-07). Pager fired and support is getting tickets.

Michael: I see alerts. 5xx rate shot from ~0.2% -> ~6.8% on api.redwood.com/v1/generate in ~10m. p95 latency also climbing. Was that canary promoted to more traffic? :eyes: 

Paula: Yes. Canary to 5% at 15:58, then promoted to 20% at 16:02. Change set included enabling pruned-kernel paths + new kv_cache_v2 opt-in. I think a config flip might be the culprit.

Raj: Pulling gateway and runtime logs now. Early corrs: lots of 502/504 at the edge, and 500s in runtime with "kernel selection failed" for a subset of hosts/variants.

Lena: Sample runtime error snippet:
```
ERROR 2026-03-07T16:10:12.123Z runtime-wrk-7 model=redwood-v1-pruned req=abc123
rpc: code=13 message="internal: kernel lookup failed (arch mismatch)" stack=".../kernel_select.go:87"
```

Michael: That smells like binary/kernel mismatch - pruned kernels were referenced but not present on all machine images. Which flag was flipped?

Paula: release notes: feature_flag enable_pruned_kernels=true for canary by default, plus a routing preference change prefer_gpu_type: a100 -> a10x fallback.

Raj: Correlation: errors concentrated on a10x fallback hosts that don't have the pruned kernel artifacts. Requests routed there hit kernel_select failure -> runtime returns 500 -> gateway reports 502 -> edge times out to user (504) after retries.

support-bot: New SRs opened: SR-4578, SR-4579. Reported by beta-apps and friendfeed - both seeing timeouts/5xx on generate. Escalated to SRE.

Paula: We accidentally promoted an assumption that kernel availability was uniform. Need immediate rollback and stop traffic promotion.

Lena: Suggested short mitigation plan:
1) pause any further promotions (set canary traffic to 0%).
2) rollback enable_pruned_kernels -> false on canary group.
3) deploy a build that removes the pruned kernel dependency or ensure artifact parity.
4) notify customers and monitor.

Michael: Can someone run the rollback? deploy-bot can reroute traffic + rollback if we provide the deploy id.

Paula: @deploy-bot rollback r-2026-03-07-canary

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: r-2026-03-07-canary -> canary-group target. Traffic scaled to 0% at 16:17:08 UTC. Job id dj-8812. Logs: https://console.redwood.local/deploys/dj-8812

Raj: Post-rollback metrics: gateway 502s dropping. 5xx rate down to ~0.5% (still slightly elevated). Need to confirm no stuck retries or queued jobs.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-031-12 (deploy regression -> increased 5xx). Severity P2. Assigned eng-oncall + eng-runtime + support.

support-bot: Support notification sent to impacted customers (SR-4578, SR-4579). Recommended message: "We've identified a deployment regression and rolled back the canary. We're monitoring and will update within 30 minutes." Using template deploy_regression_2026.

Lena: Repro steps for engineering (local/non-prod only):
1) curl the gateway hitting a10x nodes:
```
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-pruned","input":"hello"}'
```
2) tail runtime logs and watch for kernel selection failures.
3) inspect /opt/redwood/kernels on hosts for pruned kernel SHA mismatch.

Raj: Quick mitigation added: runtime routing override at 16:21 to prefer hosts labeled has_pruned_kernels=true for the affected model family, until we sync artifacts.

Michael: I'll coordinate infra to push missing kernel artifacts to the a10x fleet if we want to re-enable the flag. For now, keep enable_pruned_kernels=false globally.

Paula: Action items:
- Paula: confirm rollback closure + author postmortem (ETA 2h)
- Raj: collect logs + host list + kernel versions (ETA 30m)
- Lena: build a small test harness to simulate a10x mismatch (ETA 1h)
- Michael: patch release pipeline to check kernel metadata parity before promotion (ETA next sprint)
- Support: keep SRs updated (ongoing)

support-bot: Support updates pushed to SR-4578 & SR-4579 at 16:27 UTC.

Raj: Metrics now: 5xx ~0.18%, p95 latency back to baseline, no new spikes in last 5m. Rolling window indicates containment.

Michael: Good. Continue monitoring for 1h. I'll add a canary checklist item to verify kernel artifact parity prior to any future promotions.

Paula: Filing the postmortem template with timeline + CI gating changes. Tagging exec oncall.

oncall-bot: Reminder: next status update in 30 minutes. :alarm_clock: 

Paula: closing for now - reopen if 5xx creeps up again. Thanks everyone.
